newsitem.title: NIGERIA: New fees take effect on Nigerian bourse.
newsitem.headline: New fees take effect on Nigerian bourse.

text.p: New fees aimed at lowering transaction costs and increasing outside investment on the Nigerian stock market came into effect on Monday, an exchange official said.

The fees were first introduced in October but were suspended following a protest by stockbrokers who said that they would increase costs rather than lower them. After consultations with brokers, the exchange decided to reintroduce them this month.
Traders had no objection to the new fees when business opened on Monday.
"They have made up their mind and there is little we can do to stop them," one said.
Charges will now be graduated from between 0.1 percent and 2.5 percent from the former flat rate of three percent, officials said.
"The idea is to bring down cost of transactions to make our market competitive," said one official.
Analysts said the former falt rate made the market one of the costliest among emerging markets, and a disincentive for foreign investors.
"We are aiming at negotiable rates in the market," the official said. "That is what obtains in other markets."
